meta.title: Projects and timesheets · Clafina
meta.description: Run service projects with tasks, time and money. Get timesheets approved, then invoice the time and milestones your customer accepted.

hero.title: Every hour on the job, and every hour billed.
hero.lede: Projects with a customer, a team and a budget in hours and money. Time is approved once, costed at each person's rate and turned into invoices without typing it again.

jobs.title: See what is slipping
jobs.body: The overview shows which projects are past their end date, which are over their hours and what is waiting on you.

jobs.title: Timesheets in, and approved
jobs.body: People send their week. You approve it, or turn it back with a note, and approved weeks are locked.

jobs.title: Bill what was done
jobs.body: Invoice approved time, accepted milestones or a fixed-price schedule. Retainers and prepayments are kept too.

tour.title: One page for each project
tour.body: Progress, hours, budget and margin sit next to the team and the milestones, and the page updates as people work.
points: A milestone can need the customer's acceptance before it is billed
Gates decide when a project may move to its next stage
Profitability, budget burn and a forecast as you go

tour.title: Approve the week, not every line
tour.body: Normal weeks can be approved together. A week that looks unusual is flagged, so you only open the ones that need it.
points: Approving costs the hours at each person's rate
Billable hours become ready to invoice
Turned back weeks go to the person's Inbox to fix

tour.title: Log time where the work is
tour.body: Start a timer on a task, or add time by hand, from the phone.

items.text: A customer, a manager, a team, dates and a budget in hours and money on every project.
A billing type, a lifecycle with gates, and templates to start the next project from.
A Drive workspace for each project, and a Project dimension in the ledger.
One project table shared with manufacturing, so a production project opens there.
Tasks on a board or a list, with sub-tasks that roll up, dependencies, checklists and files.
Milestones the customer accepts before they are billed.
A notification when someone assigns you a task or mentions you.
Time logged by hand, with a timer or by import, and costed at the person's rate.
Weekly timesheets that go through approval and are locked once approved.
Timers that follow each person's own time zone.
Cost rates for each person that go beyond their base salary.
Invoices from approved time, accepted milestones and fixed-price schedules.
Stock issued to a project at cost, shown on its Materials tab.
Retainer periods that close and start again on schedule by themselves.
Late projects, projects over their hours, timesheets waiting and time to bill, with a projection.
Live screens: a change by anyone appears without a refresh.

connectsTitle: Connected to the rest of the business

connects.text: Approved time and accepted milestones become sales invoices.
Materials issued to a project leave stock at cost.
Costs and income carry the project in the ledger.
Rates come from each person's pay, and time from the timeclock.
Production projects share the same project table.
Builders run jobs and stages as projects.

faq.q: Can I bill a project by milestone?
faq.a: Yes. A milestone can need the customer's acceptance first. Once it is accepted, you draw the invoice, check it and send it.

faq.q: Can someone change a timesheet after it is approved?
faq.a: No. An approved week is locked. If something is wrong before then, you turn the week back with a note and the person fixes it.

faq.q: Can people log time from their phone?
faq.a: Yes. They can run a timer on a task or add time by hand, and send the week from there.
